title: Missing rollback plan — DDL auto-commits and Flashback cannot undo a column drop
expected_feedback: Critical: two DROP COLUMN statements with no recovery path. Oracle DDL issues an implicit COMMIT before and after each statement, so once either DROP executes the data is gone and there is no ROLLBACK. Classify both phases as restore/PITR — NOT as compensating-DDL: re-running ALTER TABLE users ADD (legacy_email VARCHAR2(255)) recreates an empty column and restores no data, so it is not a rollback. FLASHBACK TABLE ... TO SCN/TIMESTAMP is also unavailable here: Oracle cannot flash a table back across a DDL that changed its structure, and dropping a column is explicitly on that list. The safety net has to exist before the DDL runs — take a keyed snapshot (CREATE TABLE mig_bak_users_20260806 AS SELECT id, legacy_email, temp_flag FROM users) or a guaranteed restore point, and verify a backup exists. Prefer SET UNUSED COLUMN for the immediate functional removal, then DROP UNUSED COLUMNS in a maintenance window — but note SET UNUSED buys a cheaper lock, not reversibility.
violated_rule: Rollback classification provided for every phase
